newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - February 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - February 7.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Two people were killed and more than 15 wounded in clashes between police and a mob protesting against the desecration of the Koran allegedly by Christians in the town of Khanewal.
- The election commission has advised all winning candidates to submit their election expenses by February 13, failing which they might be disqualified for five years.
- U.S. intelligence officials said on Wednesday that India and Pakistan could stumble into an unwanted war that could rapidly escalate.

- The Corporate Law Authority has directed Modarabas (Islamic mutual funds) and leasing companies to submit their returns to the authority that they previously used to file with the State (central) Bank of Pakistan.
- Export of cotton has picked up after prices fell in the local markets below 2,100 rupees per maund.
- The future prime minister Nawaz Sharif made an appeal to Pakistanis living abroad to send $1,000 each to Pakistan to boost its foreign exchange reserves.
- Pakistan has cancelled a contract to buy 25,000 tonnes of sugar from India and asked it to pay compensation for not despatching the supplies in time, the Indian Express newspaper reported.
- At least 50 recruits of the Frontier Constabulary were killed when a bus, carrying them, plunged into a deep ravine.
- Nawaz Sharif is expected to meet President Farooq Leghari on February 8 to finalise details of transfer of power.
